definitions.explanation: A sport or game in which two teams pull on opposite ends of a rope, each trying to pull the other team past a center line.
A competitive back-and-forth struggle between opposing forces, such as political factions, businesses, or negotiators.

examples.japanese: {運動会|うんどうかい}で{綱引|つなひ}きをした。
examples.english: We played tug-of-war at the sports day.

examples.japanese: {綱引|つなひ}きで{白組|しろぐみ}が{勝|か}った。
examples.english: The white team won the tug-of-war.

examples.japanese: {綱引|つなひ}きはチームワークが{大切|たいせつ}だ。
{与党|よとう}と{野党|やとう}の{綱引|つなひ}きが{続|つづ}いている。
examples.english: The power struggle between the ruling and opposition parties continues.

examples.japanese: {労使|ろうし}の{綱引|つなひ}きは{長期化|ちょうきか}している。
examples.english: The tug-of-war between labor and management has dragged on.

examples.japanese: {両国|りょうこく}の{外交|がいこう}{交渉|こうしょう}は{綱引|つなひ}きの{状態|じょうたい}が{続|つづ}いている。
examples.english: The diplomatic negotiations between the two countries remain in a tug-of-war.

notes:
A compound of {綱|つな} (rope) and {引|ひ}き (pulling).

LITERAL SENSE:
One of the most popular events at Japanese {運動会|うんどうかい} (sports days) held in schools and communities. Two teams pull opposite ends of a thick rope, making it a test of collective strength.

FIGURATIVE SENSE:
Commonly used in news and politics to describe competitive back-and-forth between opposing sides. Unlike English "tug-of-war," the Japanese figurative use is standard and not at all clichéd.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {綱引|つなひ}きをする: to play tug-of-war
- {綱引|つなひ}きに{勝|か}つ/{負|ま}ける: to win/lose tug-of-war
- {政治的|せいじてき}な{綱引|つなひ}き: a political tug-of-war
- {綱引|つなひ}きが{続|つづ}く: the power struggle continues
